                    ORDER SETTING PREHEARING CONFERENCE
                   AND REQUIRING PREHEARING MEMORANDUMS

       THIS MATTER comes before hearing examiners Keven Gedko and Nicholas Rossi, on

their own motion. The Hearing Examiners FIND and CONCLUDE that a prehearing conference

should be set, and prehearing memorandums should be filed to enable the establishment of an

orderly schedule of witnesses for the forthcoming evidentiary hearing.

       IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

       1.     A prehearing conference is set for Tuesday, December 1, 2026, at 2:00 p.m. via

Zoom videoconference.

       1.     Each party shall file a prehearing memorandum by no later than 5:00 p.m.,

Thursday, December 3, 2026, identifying the following:

              a.      the names of all attorneys who will represent the party at the hearing

              b.      the names of all witnesses who have pre-filed testimony on a party’s behalf

                      and who will offer that testimony at hearing

              c.      parties that wish to be excused from the hearing

              d.      the exhibits that each party intends to present at hearing

              e.      estimates of the amount of time that the party will cross-examine each

                      witness who has pre-filed testimony and the names of witnesses for which

                         the party waives the right of cross-examination. In order to complete the

                         hearing timely, the Hearing Examiners may need to enforce time limits. 1

                 f.      any objections the party has to the admission of pre-filed testimony

                 g.      Applicant, following consultation with Staff and the other parties, shall

                         include in its prehearing memo both:

                         (i) a proposed order of presentation of all witnesses at the hearing and

                         (ii) a proposed order of cross-examination of each witness

                 h.      Parties shall indicate whether they seek to admit confidential testimony and

                         if they intend to present such information, how confidentiality will be

                         maintained as the proceeding will be streamed for public viewing.

        2.       The public hearing will be conducted via Zoom videoconferencing. An order setting

out Zoom protocols and the mechanisms by which exhibit exchange will occur will be issued

separately.

        3.       Although the protocols are spelled out in a more complete order, parties are advised

of the following procedures for testimony, exhibits, and hearing attendance:

                 a.      Pre-filed testimony and exhibits must be offered into evidence at the

                         hearing; filing those materials on the PRCe360 Case Management or

                         exchanging them via Dropbox is not sufficient to admit the testimony and

                         exhibits into the evidentiary record.

                 b.      Witnesses appearing through Zoom will appear by video, will be sworn

                         remotely by the court reporter, and should have a functioning and reliable


1 Hearing Examiners “may at their discretion limit the time for providing direct testimony or cross examination
at any public hearing if necessary to promote the proper and orderly management of such public hearing.”
1.2.2.32(G)(3) NMAC.

                     telephone line available in the event of technical problem with the Zoom

                     platform. Each party shall ensure that its participants in the hearing use the

                     computer audio and video access features in Zoom to participate – not

                     Zoom’s telephone connections.

              c.     Witnesses and attorneys shall also comply with all in-person hearing-room-

                     conduct requirements including timeliness, proper attire, and respectful

                     conduct.

              d.     When testifying, no witness should communicate with any other person,

                     including by electronic devices by text, chat, or e-mail.

              e.     Except for redirect examination, the oral testimony elicited by the party

                     presenting the witness shall consist (except for redirect examination) solely

                     of the authentication and verification of the pre-filed document. Unless

                     otherwise ordered by the Hearing Examiner, the party shall not elicit oral

                     summaries of pre-filed testimony or any other oral direct testimony.

       4.     The Hearing Examiners would like to alert the parties of a schedule change on

Friday, December 11th. The hearing will recess at noon so all PRC Employees can attend a

mandatory meeting that afternoon.
